Rashi on Gittin 64a:10:1.hebrew: תינח אמרה קיבל למה לי - לאתויי עדים שראוהו מקבלו מיד הבעל? הרי הוא בידו בפנינו, והא ודאי קבליה:
Rashi on Gittin 64a:10:1.english: That works out well [as to] "she said"; why do I [need] "he received"? - [Why does he need] to bring witnesses who saw him receiving it from the hand of the husband? Behold, it is in his hand in our presence, and surely he received it:

Rashi on Gittin 64a:10:2.english: It is [in accordance with] Rabbi Elazar - who says [that] a bill of divorce is not valid without witnesses of transmission:

Rashi on Gittin 64a:11:1.english: Why do I [need] "he tore" - That is to say, why [is it necessary] to tear it:

Rashi on Gittin 64a:11:2.english: It was a time of royal decree - when they decreed against [the observance of] the mitzvot:

Rashi on Gittin 64a:12:1.english: The third party himself is not believed - and she, when she says [it] in his name, is believed?

Rashi on Gittin 64a:14:1.english: [The] husband says [that he gave it] for divorce - [Meaning, he says:] "I gave it to the third party to hand it over to her."

Rashi on Gittin 64a:16:1.hebrew: גירשתי את אשתי נאמן - דמה לו לשקר, הרי בידו לגרשה:
Rashi on Gittin 64a:16:1.english: [A husband who says,] "I divorced my wife," is deemed credible - For why would he lie? After all, it is in his power to divorce her:

Rashi on Gittin 64a:16:2.english: Does he say, "I divorced [her]"? - He [merely] appointed [him as] an agent for delivery.

Rashi on Gittin 64a:17:1.hebrew: ונימא דחזקה שליח כו' - כיון דבעל נאמן דמסריה להאי על מנת לגרשה, נימא שחזקה שהשליח עושה שליחותו:
Rashi on Gittin 64a:17:1.english: And let us say that there is a presumption [that] an agent, etc. - Since the husband is believed that he handed [the bill of divorce] over to this [agent] in order to divorce her, let us say that there is a presumption that the agent performs his agency:

Rashi on Gittin 64a:17:2.hebrew: אסור בכל הנשים - שמא זו קרובת ארוסתו שקדש לו שלוחו היא, אא"כ חזר שלוחו לומר לו: "פלונית קדשתי לך", או "לא קדשתי לך שום אשה":
Rashi on Gittin 64a:17:2.english: [He is] prohibited from [marrying] all women - perhaps this [woman] is a relative of his betrothed whom his agent betrothed for him, unless his agent returned to tell him, "I betrothed so-and-so for you," or, "I did not betroth any woman for you":

Rashi on Gittin 64a:1:1.hebrew: או אחד מן הראשונים ואחד מן האחרונים ואחד - שלישי שנעשה עד בזו ובזו, מצטרף עמהם:
Rashi on Gittin 64a:1:1.english: Or one from the first [pair], and one from the latter [pair], and one - [a] third [witness] who became a witness in this [testimony] and in that [testimony] joins with them:

Rashi on Gittin 64a:2:1.hebrew: בעל אומר לפקדון - גט שנתון ביד שליש: בעל אומר "לפקדון נתתיו בידך", ושליש אומר "לגירושין נתת לי, שהייתי שלוחה לקבלה ונתגרשה בקבלתי", והאיש והאשה יחד בעיר:
Rashi on Gittin 64a:2:1.english: The husband says [it was given] as a deposit - [This refers to] a bill of divorce that is placed in the hand of a third party: the husband says, "I gave it into your hand as a deposit," and the third party says, "You gave [it] to me for divorce, for I was her agent for receipt, and she was divorced upon my receipt [of it]," and the husband and wife are together in the city:

Rashi on Gittin 64a:3:1.english: As he deemed him credible - when he delivered it into his hand:

Rashi on Gittin 64a:5:1.hebrew: דאיתיהיב למחילה - שאם מחלו, מחול; הלכך שליש נאמן, דכיון שהאמינו ומסר בידו, נתרצה בהבטחתו עליו למחול על ממונו ולהאמין כל מה שיאמר, אבל במילתא דאיסורא אין בידו להאמין:
Rashi on Gittin 64a:5:1.english: As it can be forgiven - For if he forgave it, it is forgiven; therefore, the third party is believed, because once he trusted him and placed [the matter] in his hands, he consented through his reliance upon him to forgive his money and to believe whatever he says; however, in a matter of prohibition, it is not in his power to believe [the third party].

Rashi on Gittin 64a:6:1.english: Monetary documents [gittei mamon] - for [the term] get simply means a document:

Rashi on Gittin 64a:7:1.hebrew: מידי גבי הדדי תניא - "וכן לגיטין, וכן לשטרות", דנימא: מדהא לשטרות דממון, קמייתא לגיטי נשים? הני תרי תנאי נינהו, ותרוייהו בממון איירי:
Rashi on Gittin 64a:7:1.english: Are they taught together - [i.e.,] "and likewise for gittin, and likewise for documents," that we should say: since this [latter clause] refers to monetary documents, the first [clause] refers to women's bills of divorce? These are two [different] Tannaim, and both of them are speaking of monetary [matters]:

Rashi on Gittin 64a:8:1.hebrew: ואמאי - בעי עדים כלל, לא בקבלה ולא באמירה, אלא באמירתו בלבד להימניה, דהא הימניה בעל:
Rashi on Gittin 64a:8:1.english: And why - does it require witnesses at all? Neither for the receipt [of the bill of divorce] nor for [her] declaration; rather, on his word alone let us believe him, for the husband trusted him.

Rashi on Gittin 64a:9:1.hebrew: מי קא נפיק גיטא מתותי ידיה - בפנינו להראותו לנו דניהמניה? הא קרעו! ואע"פ שהקרעים בידו בפנינו, אין שליש אא"כ השלישית בידו; דמיגו דאי בעי הוה עביד ביה מאי דקאמר, נאמן נמי על אמירתו, אבל זה שקרעו, אין בידו למוסרו בידה:
Rashi on Gittin 64a:9:1.english: Does the bill of divorce emerge from under his hand - before us to show it to us, [so] that we should deem him credible? Behold, he tore it! And even though the torn pieces are in his hand before us, [one] is not [deemed] a third party unless the deposited item is in his hand; for since if he wanted he could do with it what he says, he is also believed regarding his statement, whereas this one, who tore it, does not have it in his power to hand it over into her hand:

Tosafot on Gittin 64a:10:1.hebrew: תינח בפנינו אמרה - פירוש: תינח דבדין צריך שנים שיאמרו "בפנינו אמרה", ומזה לא הוה קשה מעולם; אלא "בפנינו קיבל" למה לי? נהי דלא סגי בשנים אומרים "בפנינו אמרה", כיון דנקרע הגט ולא נפיק גיטא מתותי ידיה, מ"מ למה לי "בפנינו קיבל"? לא היה צריך אלא לעדים שראוהו בידו שלם:
Tosafot on Gittin 64a:10:1.english: It works out well [as to] "in our presence she said" - Meaning: it works out well that by law two [witnesses] are needed who say, "In our presence she said [it]," and about this there was never any difficulty. Rather, why do I need "in our presence he received [it]"? Granted that it is not sufficient with two [witnesses] saying "In our presence she said [it]," since the bill of divorce was torn and no bill of divorce is produced from his possession; nevertheless, why do I need "in our presence he received [it]"? It would only have needed witnesses who saw it intact in his hand:

Tosafot on Gittin 64a:10:2.hebrew: רבי אלעזר היא דאמר עדי מסירה כרתי - ומיירי שאין העדים חתומין בו, ולכך לא סגי במה שראוהו בידו שלם, כיון שלא ראו הקבלה; אבל אם עדים חתומין בו, כשר אפי' אין כאן עדי מסירה לפנינו, דמסתמא נמסר בפני עדים ונעשה כדין, כדאמרי' בהשולח (לעיל גיטין דף לו.): אמר רבה, לא צריכא אלא לר' אלעזר דאמר עדי מסירה כרתי, תיקנו חכמים עדי חתימה דזימנין דמייתי סהדי או אזלי למדינת הים. ולקמן בהמגרש (גיטין דף פו) תנן במילתיה דרבי אליעזר גופיה: אין העדים חותמין על הגט אלא מפני תיקון העולם:
Tosafot on Gittin 64a:10:2.english: It is [in accordance with] Rabbi Elazar, who says: Witnesses of transmission effect [the divorce] - And it is dealing with [a case] where witnesses are not signed on it, and therefore it is not sufficient that they saw it in his hand intact, since they did not see the receipt; but if witnesses are signed on it, it is valid even if there are no witnesses of transmission here before us, for presumably it was transmitted in the presence of witnesses and was done properly, as we say in [the chapter] HaSholeach (above, Gittin 36a): Rabbah said: It is only necessary according to Rabbi Elazar, who says witnesses of transmission effect [the divorce]; the Sages instituted witnesses of signing because sometimes witnesses die or go overseas. And later in [the chapter] HaMgaresh (Gittin 86) we learned in the statement of Rabbi Eliezer himself: Witnesses sign a bill of divorce only for the betterment of the world:

Tosafot on Gittin 64a:17:1.hebrew: אסור בכל הנשים שבעולם - אבל לכל אדם אין לאסור לקדש ולחוש שמא זאת היא שקדש השליח, דאם איתא דנתקדשה, לא היתה חוזרת ומתקדשת; אבל האי אסור לקדש, שמא שלוחו קידש לו אחת מקרובותיה, כגון אמה ואם אמה וכיוצא בהן, ואפי' באות כל הקרובות ואמרו שלא נתקדשו, לא סמכינן אדיבורא בעלמא. ואם תאמר: יתומה קטנה תיאסר לכל אדם, שמא אביה קדשה לזה השליח? ונראה דקנסא בעלמא הוא דקנסינן ליה, שצוה לקדש סתם ולא חשש על עצמו שלא יבא לידי תקלה; אבל מן הדין מותר בכל הנשים, דאין זה חזקה גמורה, דאינה בידו להתקדש, שמא לא תתרצה, ועוד דאזלינן בתר רובא. ומ"מ מוכיח שפיר דחזקה שליח עושה שליחותו, דאי לאו הכי לא הוה ראוי לקנוס כאן. והא דפריך עלה בנזיר בפ"ב (דף יב.) מקן סתומה שפרח אחד מהם לאויר העולם, "יקח זוג לשני", ואילו שאר קינין בעלמא מיתקנן — ואע"ג דהכא קנסא בעלמא, מ"מ פריך שפיר, דהתם נמי הוה לן למקנסיה על שלא נזהר שלא יפרח, וממה דשאר קינין בעלמא מיתקנן לדידיה פריך. והא דמשני: "אמינא לך אנא, אשה דלא ניידא" — לאו משום דתיחשב כקבועה שלא תתבטל ברוב, דבדבר המתערב ואינו ניכר לא אמרינן דליהוי קבוע דידיה כמחצה על מחצה, אלא כלומר: מחמת קביעותא קנסינן טפי מבגוזל. [וע"ע תוס' נזיר יב. ד"ה אסור]:
Tosafot on Gittin 64a:17:1.english: He is prohibited from [marrying] all the women in the world - However, for any [other] man, there is no [reason] to forbid betrothing [a woman] out of concern that perhaps this is the one whom the agent betrothed, because if it were so that she had been betrothed, she would not go back and become betrothed [to someone else]; but this [sender] is prohibited from betrothing [any woman], lest his agent betrothed to him one of her relatives, such as her mother, or her mother's mother, and the like. And even if all the relatives come and say that they were not betrothed, we do not rely on mere talk. And if you will say: A minor orphan girl should be forbidden to every man, lest her father betrothed her to this agent? It appears that it is merely a penalty that we penalize him, because he instructed [the agent] to betroth [a woman] without specifying and was not concerned for himself that he might come to a stumbling block; but by [strict] law he is permitted [to marry] all women, because this is not a full-fledged presumption — since it is not in his power to betroth [a woman], as perhaps she will not consent — and furthermore, because we follow the majority. Nevertheless, [the Gemara] properly proves [from here] that there is a presumption that an agent performs his agency, for if not for this, it would not be fitting to penalize [him] here. And as for that which [the Gemara] challenges it in Nazir in the second chapter (12a) from an unspecified bird-offering pair from which one of them flew off into the open air — "he should take a mate for the second [bird], whereas all other bird-offering pairs in the world are rendered fit" — even though here it is merely a penalty, nevertheless it challenges [it] well, because there too we ought to have penalized him for not being careful that it should not fly away, and [in fact] from [the ruling] that all other bird-offering pairs in the world are rendered fit, it challenges him [i.e., the owner himself]. And as for that which [the Gemara] answers: "I am speaking to you of a woman, who is stationary" — it is not so that she should be considered 'fixed' (kavu'a) such that she would not be nullified in a majority, because in a matter that becomes intermingled and is not recognizable we do not say that its status of being fixed is treated as fifty-fifty; rather, it means: because of [her] fixedness we penalize more than in [the case of] a young bird. [See also Tosafot on Nazir 12a, s.v. "Asur"]:

Tosafot on Gittin 64a:2:1.hebrew: בעל אומר לפקדון - הא דלא נקט "בעל אומר להולכה ושליח אומר לקבלה", משום דלא שייך האי טעמא דקאמר "דאם איתא דלגירושין, לדידה הוה יהיב לה", אלא כשאומר הבעל לפקדון:
Tosafot on Gittin 64a:2:1.english: A husband says as a deposit - The reason [the Gemara] did not state [a case where] the husband says [he gave it] for delivery and the agent says [he received it] for acceptance is because this reason that [the Gemara] states — "for if it were so that [he gave it] for divorce, he would have given it to her [directly]" — only applies when the husband says [he gave it] as a deposit:

Tosafot on Gittin 64a:2:2.hebrew: ושליש אומר לגירושין - פירוש, שאומר שהיה שליח לקבלה. ומיירי כשיש שנים שמעידין "בפנינו אמרה", דשויתיה האשה שליח לקבלה, כדתנן במתני':
Tosafot on Gittin 64a:2:2.english: And the third party says for divorce - Meaning, that he says that he was an agent for receipt. And [the Gemara] is referring to [a case] where there are two [witnesses] who testify, "In our presence she said [it]," [meaning] that the wife appointed him an agent for receipt, as we learned in the Mishnah:

Tosafot on Gittin 64a:3:1.hebrew: בעל נאמן דאם איתא דלגירושין כו' - וא"ת: א"כ, מה הועילו חכמים דתקון לומר "בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם", משום דאי אתי בעל ומערער לא משגיחינן ביה? אכתי יערער, שיאמר "לפקדון נתתי". ואי דאיכא עדים דיהבינהו לגירושין, התם לא בעינן בפני נכתב. וי"ל: דלא מהימן אלא בששלשתן בעיר, דשייך האי טעמא דלדידה הוה יהיב לה. והא דפריך לרב חסדא ממתניתין, משמע דלרב הונא ניחא — היינו משום דלדידיה איכא לאוקמי בששלשתן בעיר. וא"ת: והנהו דמצרכי (לעיל גיטין דף ו.) מערסא לערסא ומשכונה לשכונה, דבעיר אחת, מה הועילו חכמים בתקנתן? וי"ל: דסברי כרב חסדא, דאמר שליש נאמן אפי' בעיר אחת; אי נמי, התם איירי כשהבעל אומר "כתבו ותנו" והלך לדרכו, דליכא למימר דלדידה הוה יהיב לה:
Tosafot on Gittin 64a:3:1.english: The husband is deemed credible, as, if it is so that [he gave it] for divorce, etc. - And if you ask: If so, what did the Sages accomplish when they instituted [that the agent must] say, "In my presence it was written and in my presence it was signed," because if the husband comes and protests we pay no attention to him? He can still protest by saying, "I gave [it] for safekeeping." And if [you say] that there are witnesses that he gave it to him for divorce, there we do not require "in my presence it was written." And one can answer that [the husband] is only deemed credible when all three of them are in [the same] city, where this reasoning applies that he would have given [it] directly to her. And as for that which [the Gemara] raises an objection against Rav Ḥisda from our Mishnah, implying that according to Rav Huna it is fine — that is because according to him, it can be established [as referring to a case] where all three of them are in [the same] city. And if you ask: According to those [authorities] who require [the declaration] (above, Gittin 6a) from bed to bed and from neighborhood to neighborhood, which is within one city, what did the Sages accomplish with their enactment? And one can answer that they hold like Rav Ḥisda, who says the third party is deemed credible even in one city. Alternatively, there it is speaking of [a case] where the husband says, "Write [it] and give [it]," and went on his way, so that one cannot say that he would have given [it] directly to her:

Tosafot on Gittin 64a:3:2.hebrew: שליש נאמן דהא הימניה - אפי' אומר הבעל שנתן לו בפני עדים, מ"מ סמך עליו, דזימנין דמייתי עדים או אזלי למדינת הים. דאין לפרש דנאמן השליש מטעם מיגו, דאי בעי עביד ביה מאי דקאמר, שיכול למוסרו לאשה כדפי' בקונטרס בסמוך; חדא, דבלא שום מיגו הימנוהו רבנן לשליש, כדמשמע בסוף זה בורר (סנהדרין דף לא.) גבי ההיא סבתא דאפקידו גבה שטרא ואמרה דפריע הוא, והימנה רב נחמן בלא שום מיגו, דכיון דאיתחזק בב"ד, "אי בעי קלתיה" לא אמרינן; ועוד, אי חשיב מיגו, לא הוה פליג רב הונא, דהיכא דאיכא מיגו מודה, כדאמרינן בסמוך: ומודה רב הונא דאי אמרה קמי דידי כו'. אלא לא חשיב מיגו, דהא אין ביד השליח למוסרו לאשה, דשמא האשה לא תתרצה לקבל הגט כיון דבעלה אומר לפקדון. לכך נראה לפרש "דהא הימניה" — כיון שמסר בידו, על דעת כן מסר לו, שיהא לגירושין אם יאמר לגירושין, אע"פ שהוא משקר. ולפי זה מהימנינן ליה לשליש אפילו בדברים העשויים להשאיל ולהשכיר, היכא דלא אמר בתורת שאילה, אלא אומר בפקדון יהבי' ניהליה:
Tosafot on Gittin 64a:3:2.english: The third party is deemed credible, as [the husband] deemed him credible - Even if the husband says that he gave it to him in the presence of witnesses, nevertheless he relied upon him, for sometimes witnesses die or go overseas. For one should not explain that the third party is deemed credible on account of a migo — [i.e.,] that if he wanted, he could do with it what he says, that he can deliver it to the woman, as Rashi explained nearby. First, because without any migo the Rabbis deemed a third party credible, as is implied at the end of [the chapter entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 31a) regarding that elderly woman with whom they deposited a promissory note, and she said that it was paid, and Rav Naḥman deemed her credible without any migo — for once it was confirmed in court, we do not say "if she wanted, she could have burned it." And furthermore, if it were considered a migo, Rav Huna would not disagree, for wherever there is a migo he concedes, as [the Gemara] says nearby: "And Rav Huna concedes that if she says 'in my presence...' etc." Rather, it is not considered a migo, for it is not in the agent's power to deliver it to the woman, since perhaps the woman will not consent to receive the bill of divorce, given that her husband says [it was given] for safekeeping. Therefore, it appears [correct] to explain "as [the husband] deemed him credible" [as follows]: Since he handed [it] over into his possession, he handed [it] over to him with this understanding — that it should be for divorce if he says [it is] for divorce, even though he is lying. And according to this, we deem a third party credible even regarding items that are normally lent or rented out, where [the owner] did not say [he gave it] as a loan, but rather says he gave it to him for safekeeping:

Tosafot on Gittin 64a:4:1.hebrew: מתיב ר' אבא הודאת בעל דין כמאה עדים דמי ושליש נאמן - משמע דנאמן אפילו כולן בעיר אחת, אע"ג דאיכא למימר דאם איתא דלאו לפקדון יהביה, הוה יהיב ליה:
Tosafot on Gittin 64a:4:1.english: Rabbi Abba raises an objection: The admission of a litigant is like one hundred witnesses, and a third party is deemed credible - This implies that [the third party] is deemed credible even when all of them are in one city, even though one could say that if it were so that he did not give it to him [merely] for safekeeping, he would have given it [directly] to him:

Tosafot on Gittin 64a:5:1.hebrew: שאני ממון דאיתיהיב למחילה - כיון שהאמינו ומסר בידו, נתרצה בהבטחתו עליו למחול על ממונו ולהאמין על כל מה שיאמר, אפי' ישקר, שהאמינו להפסידו ממונו אפילו שלא כדין; אבל במילתא דאיסורא, אין בידו להאמינו. ורב חסדא סבר דבגט נמי שליש נאמן, דעל כן נתן לו שיהא לגירושין אם יאמר לגירושין, כדפירשנו:
Tosafot on Gittin 64a:5:1.english: Money is different, as it is subject to forgiveness - Since he trusted him and placed [the matter] in his hand, he consented, in his reliance upon him, to forgive his money and to believe [him] regarding whatever he may say, even if he lies, for he trusted him to cause him a loss of his money even unlawfully; but in a matter of ritual prohibition, it is not in his power to render him believed. And Rav Ḥisda holds that with a bill of divorce as well, the third party is believed, for it was for this purpose that [the husband] gave [it] to him — that it should be for divorce if he says [it was given] for divorce, as we explained:

Tosafot on Gittin 64a:8:1.hebrew: ולהימניה לשליש - פי': אמאי צריך שנים שיאמרו "בפנינו קיבל"? אבל צריך לעולם שנים שיאמרו "בפנינו אמרה", כדפירשנו לעיל. ומשני: מי נפיק גיטא מתותי ידיה? דהנך קרעים שבידו שמא מצאו באשפה, דדוקא היכא שהגט שלם בידו, דהימניה הבעל ומסרו לו, נאמן:
Tosafot on Gittin 64a:8:1.english: And let us deem the third party credible - Meaning: why are two [witnesses] needed who say, "In our presence he received [it]"? However, two [witnesses] who say, "In our presence she said [so]," are always needed, as we explained above. And [the Gemara] answers: Does a bill of divorce emerge from beneath his hand? For [as to] those torn pieces in his hand, perhaps he found it in a trash heap; for specifically where the bill of divorce is intact in his hand, [in which case] the husband trusted him and handed it to him, is he credible:
